_note: What Haru, the straw weaver of Kaminoda, says when the farmer talks to her (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction. She has no hearts; on the bamboo hill she has her own lines (map condition). Our own lines.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Genzo says he comes for the dango. He comes for the blossoms. Don't tell him I said so.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: All these lanterns! Up in Kaminoda the only lights at night are the fireflies.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I brought a sprig of pampas from our dike for the moon table. It's the tall one.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I wrote my wish for the year on a slip of paper. If I tell you, it won't come true.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Twice in a day! Careful, people will say you've taken a liking to Kaminoda.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I'm mid-braid, so I'll talk with my hands busy. Go on.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Oh! A new face up here. I'm Haru. I weave straw: sandals, mats, rope, whatever's needed.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: If your sandals wear through, come see me before you buy some in the village.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: You found my spot. On a clear day you can count every roof in the valley from here.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: The bamboo creaks when the wind turns. Grandma said it's the hill talking in its sleep.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Rain's good for straw work: damp straw doesn't snap. My fingers say otherwise.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: The eggplants are coming along. I talk to them. Don't laugh, it works.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Morning's for the garden, before the slugs wake up and have their breakfast.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: The rack's full of sheaves! The whole lane smells of sun and straw.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Winter's for weaving. Snow boots, straw capes. The whole hamlet walks in my work.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Genzo pretends he doesn't need help with the rack. Then he lets me do all of it.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I go up the hill most afternoons. Thinking's easier with the wind in your ears.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: The persimmons in the orchard turn orange in fall. Dried, they're the best thing in winter.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: For me? Oh, this is lovely! I'll think of you every time I have one.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Thank you! That's kind of you.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Oh, thanks. I'm sure it'll be useful.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Ah... I'm not one for fish, I'm afraid. The eyes look at me.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: A rock? Is this a joke? I have plenty, thank you.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Another one? No, no, one's enough for today. Save it for yourself.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: A paper fan! I'll keep it on my workbench. Straw dust and summer heat, beware.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: You made this? It's wonderful. Can you teach me sometime?

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Still warm! I'll eat it on the hill this afternoon.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Oh, a dish. Thank you, I'll have it for supper.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Fish again... You're kind, but I'll pass this to Genzo.
